name: Classic
summary: The Classic is the round green canister that has been running on aquariums for decades. It is one open chamber you fill with whatever media you like, with no prefilter tray, electronics or clever valves to go wrong. Simple, quiet and very hard to kill.
highlights: Single open canister, so you choose and layer the media yourself
Low running costs: 8 to 20 W depending on size
Very few moving parts, so long-term reliability is its strong point
Spare parts and replacement pads are easy to find almost anywhere
bestFor: Keepers who want a no-fuss, long-lived canister for a planted tank and are happy to do a slightly messier clean now and then.
watchOut: Priming is manual on the basic version and there is no quick-release tap block, so cleaning takes more effort than on newer Eheim lines.

specs.Media: Supplied with pads or loose media depending on pack

name: Ecco Pro
summary: Ecco Pro is Eheim's compact entry canister, sized for small and mid-sized tanks. The carry handle doubles as the lever that locks the head and primes the filter, and media sits in stacked baskets, so cleaning is tidy. Power draw is very low.
highlights: Built-in priming via the handle lever, no sucking on hoses
Stacked media baskets plus a small prefilter make cleaning quick
Only 5 to 8 W running power
12/16 mm hoses on all three sizes, which suits slim lily pipes
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 60 to 300 litres where you want an easy canister that tucks into a small cabinet.
watchOut: Flow is modest for the rated tank sizes, so on a heavily planted CO2 tank choose a size up or add a circulation pump.

specs.Media: Supplied complete with pads, SUBSTRATpro and hoses

name: Experience
summary: The Experience range sits between the Classic and the Professionel. You get a square canister with media baskets and a double-tap hose block with a single release lever, so you can close both valves and lift the filter out without spilling.
highlights: Square canister is stable and packs neatly into a cabinet
Two adjustable shut-off valves on a quick-release adaptor
Supplied with mechanical and biological media, ready to run
350 model steps up to 16/22 mm hoses and over 1,000 L/h
bestFor: Mid-sized planted tanks where you want easier maintenance than a Classic without paying Professionel money.
watchOut: The 150 and 250 are fairly gentle on flow, so on a high-tech tank you may want the next size up.

specs.Taps: Double tap adaptor with release lever

name: Professionel 4+
summary: The Professionel 4+ is Eheim's mechanical flagship canister, with a lift-out prefilter under the head, separate media baskets and a self-priming pump. The Xtender button reroutes water past clogged fine pads so the biology keeps running until you get round to cleaning. The 250T and 350T versions add a 210 W heater inside the canister.
highlights: Top prefilter catches debris so the main media stays cleaner for longer
Xtender button buys a few extra days when flow starts to drop
Thermo versions (250T, 350T) hide a 210 W heater in the filter, freshwater only
16/22 mm hoses on every model, with a safety tap adaptor
Quiet ceramic shaft and adjustable flow
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 120 to 600 litres where you want solid flow, long service intervals and, if you like, no heater in the display.
watchOut: It is a tall, fairly heavy canister, so measure your cabinet, and the thermo models are not for marine use.

specs.Water type: Freshwater and marine (thermo models freshwater only)
specs.Media: Supplied complete with Eheim media and fittings

name: Professionel 5e
summary: The 5e is the electronic version of the Professionel, with a brushless pump you set up over WiFi from a browser. It can hold a constant flow as the media clogs, run a pulse mode, or drop to a quieter night flow. The 600T adds a built-in 210 W heater for freshwater tanks.
highlights: Constant-flow mode tops up pump speed as the media gets dirty
Day and night flow settings, plus pulse mode, all via WiFi in a browser
Up to 1,850 L/h with 8 L of media plus a 0.6 L prefilter on the big models
Links with Eheim's other digital kit, for example pausing flow at feeding time
600T thermo version has a 210 W heater inside, freshwater only
bestFor: Larger high-tech planted tanks where you want strong, adjustable flow and like the idea of tuning it from your phone.
watchOut: It costs a lot more than the 4+, and the WiFi setup is web-based rather than a polished app, which not everyone enjoys.

specs.Control: WiFi via web browser, no app needed

name: Professionel 3 1200XL
summary: The 1200XL (type 2080) is Eheim's big canister for very large tanks. It holds 12 litres of media plus a 1.5 litre prefilter, has two intake connections and one outlet, and rolls on built-in wheels because it is heavy once full.
highlights: 12 L of media plus a large 1.5 L prefilter
Two inlet connections and one outlet, all 16/22 mm
Flow and maintenance indicator on the head
Wheels and recessed handles for moving it around
bestFor: Very large planted displays of roughly 400 to 1,200 litres, where one filter needs to carry a lot of media.
watchOut: Media is not included and it is over 56 cm tall, and 1,700 L/h is only about 1.4 tank turnovers an hour at the top of its range, so a big planted tank will want extra circulation.

name: classicVARIO+e
summary: This is the old Classic canister rebuilt with a brushless, WiFi-controlled pump. You set the flow from a browser, and it can ramp down at night or during feeding if paired with other Eheim digital kit. It is quiet and sips power.
highlights: Brushless DC pump, adjustable in fine steps
Manual and pulse modes, set over WiFi
Uses as little as 1.7 W at low flow
Maintenance reminder by e-mail when cleaning is due
bestFor: Planted tanks of about 50 to 250 litres where you want a silent, simple canister with adjustable flow and do not need a big media load.
watchOut: Flow tops out around 510 L/h, which is modest for a high-tech tank at the top of its size range.

name: Pick-up
summary: Pick-up filters are small sponge internals that stick to the glass with suckers. The motor stays put while the sponge housing slides off for rinsing, so you do not have to unclip the whole thing or wrestle the cable.
highlights: Filter body slides off the motor for cleaning
Adjustable flow on every size
Only 3.5 to 6 W
Carbon sponge available if you want it
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, quarantine or shrimp tanks where a canister would be overkill.
watchOut: Media volume is tiny, so biological capacity is limited and the sponge needs rinsing often on a well-fed tank.

name: Aquaball
summary: The Aquaball is an internal filter with a ball-joint pump head, so you can point the outflow wherever you want surface movement. Foam cartridges handle mechanical and biological filtration, and there is a venturi if you want to add air.
highlights: Swivelling ball head for aiming the outflow
Adjustable flow, 480 to 650 L/h at the top end
Modular baskets, one to three depending on size
Venturi diffuser for extra oxygen when you need it
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech planted tanks, or as a backup filter and circulation boost on a bigger tank.
watchOut: Switch the venturi off on a CO2 tank, as the bubbles will drive off the gas you are paying for.

name: Biopower
summary: Biopower takes the Aquaball pump head and adds closed baskets filled with SUBSTRATpro, so it behaves more like a small canister hung inside the tank. It comes with a spray bar and a venturi, and the flow is adjustable.
highlights: Closed baskets of SUBSTRATpro for more biological capacity than a sponge filter
Spray bar included for gentle surface movement
Swivelling, adjustable pump head
6 to 8 W running power
bestFor: Medium planted tanks without room for a canister, or tanks with a heavier fish load that need more biology than a basic internal.
watchOut: It is a tall column inside the tank, so plan your hardscape to hide it.

name: aqua Corner Filter
summary: The aqua is a slim internal filter shaped to sit in a back corner, which leaves more open space for the scape. Filter modules clip together, so you can add another cartridge later if you need more capacity, and there is a small media box for carbon or bio media.
highlights: Corner shape keeps it out of the way of your layout
Clip-in modules, expandable with extra cartridges
Media box takes carbon, SUBSTRATpro or similar
Adjustable output and a diffuser included
bestFor: Beginner planted tanks of roughly 100 to 200 litres where you want something simple that hides in a corner.
watchOut: The listing does not give a flow figure, so on a CO2 tank you may want a separate circulation pump to be safe.

specs.Includes: Foam cartridges, 20 g carbon, diffuser and hose

name: ThermoControl
summary: ThermoControl is Eheim's standard adjustable glass heater, and it is the one many keepers have running for years without a second thought. You set it between 20 and 32 °C on the dial, and the electronics hold it within about half a degree.
highlights: Adjustable 20 to 32 °C, held to about ±0.5 °C
Red and green lamp shows when it is heating
Dry-run protection switches it off if the water drops
Ten sizes from 25 to 400 W
bestFor: Almost any planted tank, from nano to very large, where you want a proven heater you can set and forget.
watchOut: It is glass with no guard, so keep it clear of big digging fish and never lift it out while it is hot.

name: ThermoPreset
summary: ThermoPreset is fixed at 25 °C with nothing to adjust. It is slim, around 2.8 cm across, and wrapped in a plastic sleeve, so it is a sensible pick for a simple community tank or a first aquarium.
highlights: Factory set to 25 °C, no dial to knock
Plastic casing, tougher than a bare glass tube
Dry-run protection and an LED heating lamp
Slim 2.8 cm diameter
bestFor: Beginners and community planted tanks that are happy at 25 °C.
watchOut: You cannot change the temperature, so it is no good for cooler-water species or shrimp that prefer low 20s.

name: thermocontrol+e
summary: The thermocontrol+e is a glass heater with WiFi built in. You set the temperature from a browser, and it e-mails you if the water drifts more than 2 °C from target. It can also link to Eheim filters and lights to run a slightly cooler night.
highlights: Set 18 to 32 °C from a phone, tablet or computer
E-mail alert if temperature drifts by ±2 °C
Expert mode lets you calibrate against your own thermometer
Day and night temperature via Eheim's digital family
bestFor: Larger tanks where you want remote alerts about temperature, especially if you are away a lot.
watchOut: Smallest size is 150 W for 200 litres and up, and it must be mounted upright, which can be awkward in some sumps.

name: climacontrol+
summary: climacontrol+ is an inline unit that both chills and heats, controlled over WiFi. It sits on the return line after your canister, holds a set temperature anywhere from 5 to 35 °C and e-mails you if things go wrong.
highlights: Cools and heats in one inline box
Set and monitor temperature over WiFi
Warning e-mail if the water is off target for 5 minutes
Uses R290, an ozone-safe refrigerant
bestFor: Big planted tanks in warm rooms or hot climates where summer temperatures push past 28 °C.
watchOut: It is expensive, needs 500 to 800 L/h of clean filtered water through it and wants 5 cm of clear space around it for airflow.

name: compactON
summary: compactON is a family of small, quiet water pumps for moving water around a tank, a sump or a DIY filter. The smaller ones stick to the glass with suckers, and most sizes have a flow dial.
highlights: Six sizes from 300 to 5,000 L/h
Adjustable flow on all but the 5000
Ceramic shaft for quiet running
2100 and up can run outside the water as well
bestFor: Return pumps for sumps, DIY filters or water features in a planted setup.
watchOut: Output drops quickly with head height, so check the pump curve if you are lifting water a long way.

name: Universal
summary: The Universal pumps are the long-running workhorses of the Eheim range, used in sumps, trickle filters and fish houses. They can sit in the water or outside it, and a built-in prefilter protects the impeller.
highlights: Run submerged or inline outside the tank
Integrated prefilter on the intake
Four sizes from 600 to 3,400 L/h
Mounting plate included
bestFor: Sump returns or external plumbing on larger planted systems where you want a very durable pump.
watchOut: The bigger sizes draw 65 to 80 W, far more than a modern DC pump of similar output.

name: streamON+
summary: streamON+ is a compact propeller pump on a magnetic mount, used to push water around the tank rather than through a filter. It swivels on a ball joint and has a slider to throttle the outflow, and it is very frugal with power.
highlights: Magnet mount, easy to move and angle
Ball joint for full 3D positioning
Slider to reduce outflow
Only 2.5 to 12 W
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks that need extra circulation to push CO2 and nutrients into dense stem groups.
watchOut: Even the smallest moves a lot of water, so on a nano or with delicate fish, start on the lowest setting and aim it at the glass.

name: air
summary: Eheim's air pumps are small, quiet mains units with rubber feet and a hook for hanging on the tank. Each outlet has its own flow control, and the kit comes with airline, check valves and diffusers.
highlights: Individually adjustable outlets
Rubber feet to cut vibration hum
Supplied with airline, check valve and diffuser
Only 3.5 to 4 W
bestFor: Running sponge filters in shrimp tanks, or adding air overnight on a CO2 planted tank.
watchOut: Keep it off during the CO2 photoperiod, since surface agitation from the bubbles will strip out CO2.

name: reeflexUV
summary: reeflexUV is an inline UV clarifier that goes on your canister's return hose. A reflector inside bounces the UV back through the water, so it gets more done per watt than a plain unit, and it kills free-floating algae that turns water green.
highlights: Fits inline on the filter return
Internal reflector boosts effective UV dose
Clears green water from suspended algae
Three sizes to match tank volume and filter flow
bestFor: Planted tanks prone to green water, or anyone wanting a bit of extra clarity and pathogen control.
watchOut: It does nothing for algae growing on plants or glass, and the lamp needs replacing about once a year.

name: reeflexUV+e
summary: The reeflexUV+e is the WiFi version of the reeflexUV. You can run it constantly, on a daily schedule or linked to other Eheim devices, and it tells you by e-mail when the lamp is due for a change.
highlights: Constant, daily cycle or coupled modes over WiFi
Booster mode for a short, intense treatment
Lamp change reminder by e-mail
Switches off automatically when you open it to change the lamp
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want UV only for set hours, or want it tied into an Eheim digital setup.
watchOut: It costs about twice as much as the standard reeflexUV for the same job, so only worth it if you will use the scheduling.

name: skim350
summary: The skim350 is a small powered surface skimmer that clips to the glass and sucks the oily film off the top of the water into a sponge. It runs on its own pump, so it does not need to be plumbed into your filter.
highlights: Clears surface film for better gas exchange
Self-contained, no filter connection needed
Sponge catches the debris, rinse and reuse
5 W power draw
bestFor: Planted tanks up to 350 litres that get a stubborn protein film on the surface, which is common with CO2 and heavy feeding.
watchOut: It is a visible box in the tank, and the sponge needs rinsing often or it stops skimming.

name: powerRGB
summary: powerRGB is a low-voltage RGB LED bar meant to sit alongside your main light and add colour. Paired with the RGBcontrol+e controller (sold separately) you can blend colours, run sunrise and sunset, and add moonlight.
highlights: Adds red, green and blue to lift plant and fish colour
Three lengths for tanks from about 79 to 125 cm
Roughly 1,550 to 2,170 lumens
Low-voltage, 21.9 to 30.7 W
bestFor: Tanks that already have a white main light and where you want richer reds and greens, or smooth dawn and dusk.
watchOut: It is a supplementary light, not a full planted-tank light on its own, and the colour control needs an extra controller.

name: aquafamily
summary: aquafamily is a 66 litre starter set with a lid-mounted RGBW LED you can program over WiFi, plus a corner filter, a preset heater and a thermometer. The app guides families through feeding and maintenance.
highlights: RGBW LED with sunrise, sunset, clouds and moonlight, set via app or browser
Comes with aqua 160 corner filter and 100 W thermopreset heater
Polished glass edges and a base frame
App reminders for feeding, water changes and filter cleaning
bestFor: A first aquarium for a family, or a tidy low-tech planted tank on a sturdy sideboard.
watchOut: The lid light is aimed at general viewing, so demanding carpeting plants will struggle without extra light.

specs.Includes: LED lid, aqua 160 filter, thermopreset 100 W heater, thermometer

name: vivaline LED
summary: vivaline LED is a complete aquarium and cabinet set with a lid, LED light, Biopower internal filter and heater. A swappable decorative panel on the cabinet lets you change the look to match your room.
highlights: Tank, cabinet, LED lid, filter and heater all included
126 L comes with a Biopower 160, 180 L with a Biopower 200
Cabinet front panel can be swapped even with the tank full
Pine, oak grey, white or anthracite finishes
bestFor: Low-tech community planted tanks where you want everything matched and ready to set up.
watchOut: The single 13 or 17 W LED is fine for easy plants, but a stem-heavy or carpeted scape will want a stronger light and a canister.
